title_en: The City of Eight — the subtle body
answer: Yes — Abhinavagupta explicitly equates the body with the City of Eight (puryaṣṭaka) and defines body-ness (dehatva) as the 'I'-sense (ahaṃtā / ahaṃbhāva): to 'burn the body' is to destroy that I-sense, and that is liberation. The clearest full-stack witness is Tantrasāra 13.24; Tantrāloka 15.234–236 states the same equation, and Tantrāloka 24.20–21 says that with the puryaṣṭaka gone there is no heaven or hell — i.e. it is the transmigrating subtle vehicle. Tantrāloka 9.204–205 ties it to the six kañcukas that contract the knower (the aṇu).

claims.claim: The body IS the City of Eight, and its body-ness is the 'I'-sense; burning the body means destroying that I-sense.

evidence.label: Tantrasāra 13.24
evidence.quote_iast: evaṃ sthite uttarābhimukham upaviśya dehapuryaṣṭakādau ahambhāvatyāgena dehatāṃ dahet / saṃnidhāv api paradehavat adehatvāt tato nistaraṅgadhruvadhāmarūḍhasya dṛṣṭisvābhāvyāt yā kila ādyā spandakalā saiva mūrtiḥ
evidence.quote_en: Thus standing, facing north one should sit, burning body-ness in body-city-eight and the rest by I-feeling abandonment; from nearness as another's body, from bodilessness — then mounted on the waveless steady abode, from gaze-nature — which indeed is the first throb-digit — that alone is the form.

evidence.label: Tantrāloka 15.234–236
evidence.quote_iast: tena mantrāgninā dāho dehe puryaṣṭake tathā / dehapuryaṣṭakāhantāvidhvaṃsādeva jāyate / nahi sadbhāvamātreṇa deho@sāvanyadehavat / ahantāyāṃ hi dehatvaṃ sā dhvastā taddaheddhruvam
evidence.quote_en: By that mantra-fire the burning is in the body, the city of eight; liberation arises precisely from destroying the I-ness of the body-city-of-eight. For it is not a body by mere existence, like another body; body-ness lies in the I-sense — that, destroyed, is verily burnt.
evidence.translation_note: Verbatim. Our rendering shown; a machine-proposed L2 also exists for this verse (gloss-level, UNREVIEWED).

claims.note: Abhinavagupta's point is stronger than 'a subtle body exists': the deha is defined by ahaṃtā, so 'burning the body' in initiation is the destruction of the ego-sense, not of flesh.

claims.claim: The City of Eight is the transmigrating vehicle: with it gone, heaven and hell and the rest do not obtain.

evidence.label: Tantrāloka 24.20–21
evidence.quote_iast: eṣā sāṃnyāsikī dīkṣā puryaṣṭakaviśodhanī / puryaṣṭakasyābhāve ca na svarganarakādayaḥ
evidence.quote_en: This is the renunciate initiation, purifying the city-of-eight; and with the puryaṣṭaka gone, no heaven, hell, and the rest.

claims.note: Ritual corollary: the purificatory dīkṣā targets the subtle vehicle; without it the karmic destinations (heaven/hell) have no support.

claims.claim: The six kañcukas contract the knower situated 'in the body, the city of eight, and the rest'; that contracted knower is the aṇu.

evidence.label: Tantrāloka 9.204–205
evidence.quote_iast: māyā kalā rāgavidye kālo niyatireva ca / kañcukāni ṣaḍuktāni saṃvidastatsthitau paśuḥ / dehapuryaṣṭakādyeṣu vedyeṣu kila vedanam / etatṣaṭkasasaṃkocaṃ yadavedyamasāvaṇuḥ
evidence.quote_en: Māyā, kalā, rāga, vidyā, kāla and niyati — these six are called the coverings; in their presence the knower is the bound one (paśu). Knowing occurs, indeed, in the knowables beginning with the body, the city of eight; that contraction by this sixfold set is what is unknown to him — he is the atom (aṇu).
evidence.translation_note: Verbatim. Our rendering shown; a machine-proposed L2 also exists for this verse (gloss-level, UNREVIEWED).

claims.note: This links the subtle body to the kañcuka doctrine: the puryaṣṭaka is where the contracted (aṇu) experience of the bound self is located.

claims.claim: The eight constituents are the five tanmātras (sound, touch, form, taste, smell) together with manas, ahaṃkāra and buddhi.

evidence.label: Tantrāloka 24.18–19
evidence.quote_iast: pūjayitvā śrutisparśau rasaṃ gandhaṃ vapurdvayam / dhyahaṃkṛtī manaśceti brahmādiṣvarpayetkramāt
evidence.quote_en: Having worshipped sound, touch, taste, smell, the two forms, and the I-maker and mind, one should offer them in order to Brahmā and the rest.
evidence.translation_note: R-tier: the verse's list is compressed and does not name all eight constituents explicitly; the classical enumeration (5 tanmātras + manas + ahaṃkāra + buddhi) is supplied by the tradition and is not invented here.

claims.note: Model, not doctrine: the count (eight) is attested by the term puryaṣṭaka; the exact partition per this verse is uncertain and flagged.

levels_report.note: What the corpus actually holds for these witnesses (not what we wish it held).
